purpose: Rigid integrated project-control data model for OhmBoy.
rules: Every financial record must map to a phase code and SOV line.
Every risk must include probability, impact, owner, mitigation, watch date, trigger date, and linked items.
Every packet must be linkable to the objects it affects.
All objects must be searchable by ID, status, owner, phase code, SOV line, vendor, schedule activity, and keyword.
Audit log records create/update/status changes.
High-level financial summary numbers must identify the report/source they came from and carry matching color-code references.
Open PO remaining must flow into left-to-spend and PO forecast must be considered in EAC review.
Billed and forecast billing records must be aged by payment terms and tied back to SOV lines.
Financial simulations must update the same report buckets that feed the high-level overview.
Change Order log rows must show open C/O value and projected contract value if approved.
Simulation buttons must use delegated click binding and direct global handlers so visible buttons cannot fail due to late DOM binding.
The Executive Cockpit is the primary navigation surface; sidebar view tabs are hidden but retained for routing.
Sidebar visibility is a UI shell preference and must not affect cockpit module routing or report state.
Back to Cockpit must be globally available and route to the cockpit view without depending on sidebar visibility.
Branch resolution requires a note before the branch can be marked resolved.
Resolution notes must be stored on the branch and surfaced in the Audit Trail as a searchable/auditable column.
Raw code, JSON payloads, and drilldown developer drawers must not be visible in the user-facing UI.
Record clicks must not open developer payload popups; actionable controls remain functional.
Audit Trail must keep Detail and Resolution Note in separate columns.
Audit Trail branch status must reflect the current Triage Packet branch status when a branch is linked.
Branch resolution must not create a standalone audit row or new AUDIT ID.
Resolution notes and resolved date/time are lifecycle columns on the related audit row.
Standalone legacy Branch resolved audit rows must be hidden from the Audit Trail display.
Resolution note displayed in the Audit Trail must fall back to the linked Triage branch if the audit row lacks the field.
Resolving a branch must enrich the existing audit row when a matching row exists.
No standalone audit row should be created for branch resolution.
Resolution note source of truth is the Branch Resolution Ledger.
Resolve Branch must write branch status, note, resolved date/time, and ledger entry before rendering.
Final Close must sync resolved branches into the ledger before closing the packet.
Audit Trail must display notes from ledger first, then branch fallback, then audit row fallback.
